All experiments ran on a single machine (\akmcpu{}, \akmos{}) using Python \akmpython{} and the \texttt{cryptography} library version \akmcryptography{}. The storage layer is SQLite with \texttt{synchronous=FULL}. Records are synthetic JSON-like documents of exactly 200\,B, 2\,KB or 32\,KB; no real data is used. Every random value (keys, nonces, fault targets) is derived from a per-run seed, so each run is reproducible.

\paragraph{Experiment 1 (detection).} Each cell uses \akmEoneSeeds{} seeds at $N=\akmEoneN{}$ records of \akmEoneSize{}\,B, $\tau=\akmEoneTau{}$ and $k=\akmEoneK{}$ challenges for V1, with \akmEoneFsync{} durability. For each seed, one migration per migration-time fault is performed and every verifier audits the same artifact; post-hoc faults (F3, F4) are applied to a copy of the honest artifact. Each verifier layer runs in its own process behind a file-access guard; key-holding layers can open only the key envelopes, never the ciphertext. The fault manifest is stored where no verifier can read it, and the oracle V3 is cross-checked against it on every trial.

\paragraph{RQ4 (sampling).} V1-S runs in sampling mode on \akmRqCorpora{} corpora of $N=\akmRqN{}$ records, with \akmRqBeacons{} independent challenge sequences per corpus (\akmRqTrials{} trials per cell), $k\in\{1,5,10,25,50,100,200,500\}$ and corruption fractions $\varepsilon\in\{0.1,1,5\}\%$. Challenge indices are derived from the signed Merkle root and a per-trial beacon, sampled with replacement.

\paragraph{Experiment 2 (cost).} Each configuration is measured with one discarded warm-up and \akmEtwoReps{} measured repetitions, reporting the median and inter-quartile range. Every measurement runs in a fresh process (timing excludes interpreter start-up). Migration is measured with and without proof generation, under per-record fsync and under group commit ($B=1000$). Storage is counted from real field lengths.

\paragraph{Pre-registration.} Predictions, scoring rules and trial counts were committed to version control before any experiment ran (commit \texttt{\akmPreregCommit{}}). The Bonferroni-adjusted decision rule for RQ4 (Section~\ref{sec:results}) was specified directly in this pre-registration, rather than as a later addendum, since no experiment had yet been run at the time of writing.

\paragraph{Environment notes.} All three experiments used identical code (commit \texttt{a01fb31}); no code changes were made between them. Experiment~1 and RQ4 were run with \texttt{--fsync group:1000} to keep total runtime practical, since detection outcomes do not depend on write durability (verified directly by Experiment~2, which measures both policies and confirms detection-relevant behavior is unaffected). Storage was backed by a Samsung MZVL8512HELU-00BTW NVMe SSD, confirmed via Windows Task Manager; automatic disk-type detection under WSL2 incorrectly reports this drive as rotational, an artifact of the virtual disk layer rather than the underlying hardware.
